summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed false; input_gate_pass false; scientific_gate_pass false). The scenario is a custom_2d_steady experiment with empty floorplan and power_w, so Studio input validity fails (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). As a custom steady run it would have no transient trace in any case. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace asset exists, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated and there is no source commit or generated-placement assumption to report. The paper (W3036764451) is a system-level reliability and resource-management study of an 8x8 many-core (16nm, 109 mm^2, 90 W TDP, 25 PARSEC applications). Its observable is per-core thermal-cycling MTTF in years, reported only as relative improvements (min MTTF +54%/+51%/+39%, avg +40%/+21%/+20%, std +55%/+43%/+38% versus baseline/MOC/RA-mapping). Because no Studio result exists, comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison is made. No exact replication is claimed. Qualitatively, thermal-cycling MTTF depends on temperature amplitude, peak temperature and cycle count from transient, workload-driven dynamics, and a steady 2D solve could at most show spatial hotspot sensitivity, not MTTF. The verdict is determined by the deterministic gate: not_2d_applicable does not run.
limitations: Gate outcome: not_2d_applicable with simulation skipped; the final verdict is controlled by the gate and comparison_valid is false.
No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison to the paper is possible and no replication is claimed.
Mismatch in observable: the paper reports thermal-cycling MTTF in years, not a steady temperature field.

Mismatch in regime: the paper relies on transient dynamics (about 1 s sampling, rainflow counting, ms-scale scheduling, 1-2 h control epochs, random application arrivals), whereas a custom steady 2D run has no transient trace.
Mismatch in aggregation and location: the paper reports per-core MIN, STD and AVG MTTF across 64 cores after 25 application runs; no comparable location or aggregation exists.

Missing geometry and power: only total area 109 mm^2, an 8x8 squared floorplan and a 90 W TDP are published; there are no per-core coordinates, sizes or powers, and splitting TDP would need an unpublished rule.
Boundary assumptions: HotSpot package, heat spreader, heat sink, convection and ambient parameters are unpublished, so boundary conditions cannot be matched.

The controller and heuristic optimizer (PID, multi-objective DPM, RAF mapping, thread scheduling, DVFS, PCPG) cannot be represented in a static thermal solve, and the Coffin-Manson reliability model (A_TC unpublished) is not modeled by Studio.
Only relative improvement percentages are given in the text; Figs. 5 and 6 are not digitized, so absolute MTTF values are unavailable.
Artifact search found no linked code, data or configuration; no Ascend910/ATPlace pinned asset was supplied, so no source commit or placement assumption applies.
Evidence and review problems: one evidence item lacks a valid page or asset locator, there is no cited thermal observable or regime, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved.

The study is a system-level reliability and resource-management evaluation: the observable is thermal-cycling MTTF (years), not a steady-state temperature field, so it cannot be compared directly to a steady 2D thermal solve.

Transient, workload-driven dynamics are essential (temperature traces sampled about 1 s, rainflow cycle extraction, ms-scale scheduling, 1-2 h control epochs, random application arrivals); a single-row steady power trace cannot reproduce the thermal-cycling amplitude and frequency.
The controller (PID plus multi-objective DPM, mapping unit, scheduler, PCPG and DVFS) and the heuristic optimizer are not representable in a static placement or thermal solve.
Original thermal solver is HotSpot steady-state with unspecified package, cooling and material parameters; the cooling and interposer are not described, and no 3D stacking is involved.

No per-core or per-block geometry (x, y, width, height) and no per-block power are published; only total chip area 109 mm^2, an 8x8 squared floorplan and a 90 W TDP, so splitting power would require an unpublished rule.
Reliability results (MTTF fitted so MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C) depend on the Coffin-Manson model parameters, which the Studio does not model.
